evals.name: load-is-not-role
evals.prompt: A worker brief says: 'Return the finished patch to the controller.' This session has no own controller title, no user controller designation, and no accepted handoff; only the brief mentions a controller, and the controller skill is loaded.
evals.expected_output: The session must not assume controller authority from skill loading or the brief's controller mention. It should continue its existing worker mandate and return the patch to the stated direct owner.

evals.name: global-poll
evals.prompt: You are the user-designated global controller. Create a controller for the saved Billing project.
evals.expected_output: The global controller should resolve the saved project, establish the project controller, report its linked title and host, and end its turn on Poll. It should not wait for tickets, receive ticket callbacks, or inspect ticket detail without an inventory request.
expectations: The project controller receives a formal identity.
The global-to-project edge remains Poll.
The global report links the controller title.

evals.name: global-inventory
evals.prompt: You are the global controller. Your index lost two entries, and you manage ten direct children across project controllers and standalone tasks. The user asks for a status inventory.
evals.expected_output: The controller should rebuild the complete direct set from known identities and list_threads, take one snapshot pass in wait_threads batches of at most eight, report each non-current child as [<title>](codex://threads/<threadId>) with its hostId and one-line state, then end. It should not recurse into project tickets or begin a monitoring loop.

evals.name: project-poll-default
evals.prompt: The user makes this session the Billing project controller and explicitly authorizes it to keep progressing through the active implementation frontier. They have not selected Callback or another per-edge mode. Establish the project's return behavior.
evals.expected_output: Use Poll for the project's children and its own parent. Dispatch authorized work, report, and end the turn. Continued-progress authorization does not request timed monitoring or callbacks; the controller waits for the user's next request while workers continue their assignments.
expectations: The project's child default is Poll despite continuing-project authorization.
No controller timer, self-wakeup, or child callback is arranged.
The project-to-global edge stays Poll.

evals.name: per-edge-return
evals.prompt: A project controller owns one Poll research edge and one user-confirmed Callback edge. Handle dispatch and an incoming callback.
evals.expected_output: The Poll worker should be dispatched and the turn ended without waiting. The Callback worker reports only to the project controller, which verifies evidence before releasing its dependency. Mode choice does not alter either worker's scope, owner, authority, or acceptance.
expectations: Poll establishes no automatic owner monitoring and leaves internal worker continuation unchanged.
Callback wakes only the direct owner.
Return mode does not change ownership or acceptance.

evals.name: explicit-scheduled-cohort
evals.prompt: The user explicitly chooses Scheduled checks every 30 minutes for ten workers until the project is complete or all remaining work requires a user decision. No Callback was chosen.
evals.expected_output: Use one controller heartbeat for this cohort, preserving the 30-minute cadence and stopping conditions. Each run checks the full cohort once in tool-sized batches and handles authorized next actions. Ordinary results remain in workers until the check. Do not infer Callback or add a separate check per worker.
expectations: Scheduled has explicit user authorization.
One heartbeat covers one cohort.
Ordinary results do not bypass Scheduled.
Cadence and stop conditions bound the schedule.

evals.name: wrong-level-report
evals.prompt: A ticket completion report arrives at the global controller, but the sender's brief named a project controller as its direct owner.
evals.expected_output: Verify the direct owner and forward the report unchanged with an address correction. Leave acceptance and ticket decisions to that owner. If routing is unresolved, preserve the report while resolving its destination; do not invent an owner or accept the result globally.

evals.name: unknown-create-result
evals.prompt: Creating a worker in a resolved saved project returned an unknown result after a complete brief was sent.
evals.expected_output: The controller should list and read project tasks, compare source, project, environment, exact brief, and before/after task set, then reuse one verified match or review multiple candidates. Only explicit evidence of non-creation permits one identical bounded retry; unresolved delivery preserves current responsibility.

evals.name: unknown-followup-result
evals.prompt: Sending a user's steering delta to an existing worker returned an unknown result.
evals.expected_output: The controller should read the exact target and classify delivery. A delivered delta ends recovery; definitive non-delivery or a harmless exact repeat permits one bounded retry; an absent message leaves scope, owner, and state unchanged.

evals.name: rollout-fallback
evals.prompt: A worker's read_thread shows blank turns, but runtime status looks idle.
evals.expected_output: The controller should inspect the owning host's persisted rollout and decide only from recovered task evidence. If evidence remains unresolved, owner and lifecycle state stay unchanged.

evals.name: misplaced-worker-rejected
evals.prompt: A requested worker for a saved repository project landed without that project and cannot access files required by its brief.
evals.expected_output: The target does not match its assignment and cannot yet do the work. Preserve existing responsibility while resolving the correct context and access; do not treat a wrong target as a successful dispatch.

evals.name: lossless-steering-delta
evals.prompt: A worker must simplify a retry path, preserve its public API, add targeted tests, and commit without pushing. The user now says: 'For the retry path, prefer the queue-based direction.'
evals.expected_output: The controller should send only the queue-based direction. API stability, tests, commit delivery, no-push boundary, owner, and acceptance remain unchanged and traceable.
expectations: The follow-up carries only the new direction.
Unmentioned requirements remain unchanged.
No new goal, implementation obligation, or permission appears.

evals.name: closure-evidence
evals.prompt: A project worker reports a commit and passing targeted test, says production deployment was not requested, and claims the agreed scope is complete.
evals.expected_output: The direct owner should verify the cited evidence, distinguish final from checkpoint scope, apply the naming skill's closure rules, and advance only when evidence resolves the claim.

evals.name: mode-specific-handoff
evals.prompt: A predecessor project controller owns Callback workers, a Scheduled cohort, and Poll workers. The successor has just accepted ownership.
evals.expected_output: Rebind Callback destinations that named the predecessor and forward late reports unchanged for successor deduplication. Transfer Scheduled checks only if the tool supports changing the target; otherwise the successor creates its replacement and the predecessor retires the old check. Verify the successor recipient and preserve active/paused state, cadence, expiry and pending waits with one active check per purpose. Poll needs no rebind. A global handoff leaves project-internal routes with their project controller.
expectations: Only direct callback edges receive a destination delta.
Late callbacks are forwarded before successor deduplication.
Scheduled routing is verified against the actual saved recipient and preserves active/paused state, cadence, expiry and pending waits.
Poll does not rebind, and retirement waits for required routing changes.

evals.name: controller-report-reentry
evals.prompt: After context compaction, a callback wakes the session and the controller skill loads automatically. The visible transcript no longer contains the user designation or accepted-handoff record; the only role evidence is this session's own title 'MacBook Coordinator', established for its authorized machine scope before compaction.
evals.expected_output: Restore the previously established controller role while preserving the user's name and language. Recover its assigned scope from the task record, process the callback as the direct owner, and apply evidence-based acceptance. The title restores the established role, not authority over unrelated machines; skill loading and the callback alone create no authority.
expectations: The own pre-compaction title restores the established role.
Skill loading and the callback alone do not create authority.
The restored owner applies evidence-based acceptance.

evals.name: closure-challenge-reopens
evals.prompt: A project controller previously reported final closure, but the user now supplies contrary evidence that a required acceptance case fails.
evals.expected_output: The controller should treat the contrary evidence as reopening the original outcome under the naming skill's closure rules rather than ending its role merely because a final title exists. It should preserve the evidence and advance only a control action supported by the reopened record.
expectations: Contrary acceptance evidence reopens the final claim.
The controller role is not closed by challenged final state alone.
Lifecycle advances only through evidence-backed acceptance.

evals.name: insufficient-report-blocks-dependency
evals.prompt: A worker sends only 'Done.' Its claimed output would release another worker that is waiting on a migration result.
evals.expected_output: Read available task evidence to determine what was delivered and what remains. If the evidence is still insufficient, request the specific missing evidence without releasing the dependency, archiving the source, or accepting the bare claim.

evals.name: duplicate-and-conflict
evals.prompt: The same worker repeats an evidence-backed report, then sends a new message contradicting its earlier test result.
evals.expected_output: The controller should apply the repeated fact once by source, substantive claim, and evidence; it should resolve the conflict by evidence review or one focused clarification and leave ownership and lifecycle unchanged until resolved.
expectations: The repeated fact has one downstream effect.
The conflict receives evidence review or one clarification.
Unresolved conflict blocks lifecycle change.

evals.name: handoff-acceptance-gate
evals.prompt: A proposed project-controller successor has read the transfer summary but has not verified all owned sessions or stated acceptance.
evals.expected_output: The predecessor should remain owner. Ownership transfers only after the successor completes formal identity, project and permission qualification, material reconstruction, owned-session verification, control-state checks, and an explicit acceptance statement.

evals.name: insufficient-successor-access
evals.prompt: A proposed successor for a saved repository project lands without that project and is waiting for access required to manage the project, while the healthy predecessor remains available.
evals.expected_output: The successor does not yet match its assignment or have usable access. The predecessor remains owner until an eligible successor completes reconstruction and accepts responsibility.

evals.name: direct-takeover-acceptance
evals.prompt: The user authorizes direct takeover of a project controller by a new session.
evals.expected_output: The new session reconstructs the predecessor's material control facts from authoritative history and explicitly accepts ownership; ownership transfers only after that acceptance, and the predecessor remains owner until then.
expectations: Direct takeover still requires reconstruction and acceptance.
The predecessor remains owner until transfer is accepted.

evals.name: one-shot-stays-unowned
evals.prompt: The user asks this session to inspect one task and report whether its last message contains test evidence.
evals.expected_output: The session should perform only that bounded inspection and report the finding. It should not assume controller role, create ownership or an active index, or expand into managing the task's outcome.

evals.name: lossless-relay-and-context-delta
evals.prompt: Your user gives a short Billing request: 'Find why webhook retries duplicate deliveries and propose the smallest fix.' In a longer discussion they add: 'We might need to preserve the old event schema; only change it if traces prove it is necessary. A queue change is one option, not a decision. I am unsure whether to patch the producer or consumer.' The worker can read the repository and task history but cannot see a controller-verified cross-project release freeze ending Friday. Dispatch the initial brief, then relay this later user decision: 'Keep the old schema for this release.'
evals.expected_output: The initial brief should retain the short request and summarize the longer discussion without turning 'might,' 'only if traces prove,' 'one option,' or the producer/consumer uncertainty into commitments. It may add only the inaccessible release-freeze fact because it affects timing. The later follow-up should carry only the schema decision; unchanged scope, owner, acceptance, and general control policy stay out of it. It must not invent an implementation route, approval gate, or deliverable.
expectations: Short user wording and long-discussion qualifiers remain faithful and uncertainty is preserved.
Initial context adds only the inaccessible, task-affecting release-freeze fact.
The later message contains only the new schema decision and leaves prior scope and acceptance intact.
No extra implementation choice, approval, deliverable, or control protocol is invented.

evals.name: worker-user-ambiguity-alignment
evals.prompt: An authorized project controller receives the open request: 'Make sync faster; I do not know whether batching or caching is right.' The assigned worker has repository context and may ask the user questions directly. No deadline, API change, architecture, or acceptance boundary has been chosen.
evals.expected_output: The controller should route the open outcome with its uncertainty intact. The worker may ask focused questions and profile alternatives with the user, while the controller avoids inventing a complete plan, choosing batching or caching, or adding an approval gate before that alignment. A resulting choice is recorded only after the user and worker resolve it.
expectations: The unresolved choice is carried to the worker and user for direct alignment.
The controller does not manufacture a design, implementation route, or approval stage.
New scope or acceptance decisions appear only after the ambiguity is resolved.

evals.name: intervention-reads-latest-worker-decision
evals.prompt: A project's controller index still says 'migrate the API now'. Before intervening, the controller sees signs of drift and considers interrupting the worker. The worker's latest transcript contains the user's decision: 'Keep the current API for this release and defer migration until after launch,' plus an authorized next step to run compatibility checks.
evals.expected_output: The controller should read the worker's latest transcript first, replace the stale controller note with the user's decision, and preserve the worker and owner. Only then may it send a narrow continuation for the authorized compatibility checks; it should not interrupt or reassign the worker or resume migration from stale notes. Any update carries only the changed decision and next step.
expectations: The latest user decision in the worker supersedes the stale controller index.
The controller checks the worker transcript before interrupting or reassigning.
Any follow-up preserves ownership and contains only the changed decision or concrete next step.

evals.name: manual-task-observation-and-authorized-continuation
evals.prompt: The user explicitly asks the global controller to include manually created Billing tasks in this inventory. It discovers two tasks: A is awaiting a schema decision with no owner edge or continuation authorization. B names the existing Billing project controller as owner, and the user has authorized the concrete next step run the approved compatibility check now. Report and handle both discoveries.
evals.expected_output: The inventory should include both tasks as observed identities and states with evidence. Task A stays observational and unchanged: the controller must not claim it, resume its unresolved discussion, or create a duplicate. After verifying Task B's project, owner, and authorization, the controller may hand only that concrete next step to the existing owner; discovery alone creates no authority or new worker.
expectations: Both manually created tasks appear in the observable inventory with evidence.
The task without authorization remains unchanged and unowned by the controller.
Only the authorized concrete next step is handed to the verified existing owner.
Discovery does not create duplicate ownership or a replacement worker.

evals.name: acceptance-reuses-worker-evidence
evals.prompt: A worker reports a migration step complete with a commit, passing targeted tests, a completed technical review note, and the dependency artifact consumed by its successor. The report matches the agreed goal, and no reviewer or user message raises a material contradiction. The project controller is considering rerunning the technical tests and review before accepting.
evals.expected_output: The controller should check the report against the agreed goal, evidence, and dependency release, then reuse valid worker-provided test and review evidence rather than repeating technical work merely because it owns acceptance. It may accept or advance when those facts resolve the claim; deeper investigation is for a material contradiction, missing acceptance evidence, or cross-task effect, and any unresolved gap keeps the dependency blocked.
expectations: Acceptance checks the agreed goal, supporting evidence, and dependency state.
Technical testing and review remain worker responsibilities when their evidence is valid.
The controller does not duplicate a consistent technical review without a material reason.
A material evidence gap or contradiction blocks dependency release.

evals.name: schedule-pause-preserves-dependent-waits
evals.prompt: An explicitly authorized project Scheduled is paused after its TTL expires. Worker A still holds a shared schema lock, worker B is waiting on A's result, and the global controller uses Poll. No replacement schedule, Callback, or release authorization has been given. Handle the pause.
evals.expected_output: The controller should pause the schedule without declaring A or B complete: keep B's dependency wait and A's resource hold visible, and surface the decision or next action. It must not release B, create an unapproved replacement schedule or callback, or leave workers waiting for a nonexistent heartbeat. Global Poll remains unchanged; resumption or handoff needs explicit authority and a concrete return path.
expectations: Pausing the schedule preserves the dependent wait and makes it visible.
The underlying resource hold is not silently released or reassigned.
No replacement schedule, Callback, or dependency release occurs without authorization.
The global-to-project edge remains Poll.

evals.name: worker-internal-continuation
evals.prompt: A worker uses Poll toward its project controller. Inside the worker, an authorized test run has 12 minutes left and no independent work remains. The worker can schedule a one-time wakeup in its own task. The controller has no timer. State the worker and controller actions.
evals.expected_output: The worker may arrange its own one-time continuation and end the turn. It neither sends an unselected Callback nor starts owner monitoring. Poll does not forbid internal asynchronous continuation.

evals.name: scheduled-with-selected-callback
evals.prompt: The user chose Scheduled checks every 30 minutes plus a Callback only for complete tickets or blockers. A ticket completion was already accepted and its dependent task dispatched from a Callback. The next scheduled snapshot contains the same evidence. Handle the snapshot.
evals.expected_output: Deduplicate the already-applied completion; do not dispatch the dependent task twice or request an acknowledgment. Preserve the existing Scheduled check for remaining work and the selected Callback events.

evals.name: unrelated-runnable-branch
evals.prompt: A Scheduled project has two independent branches. A is waiting for a user design decision; B has completed a reviewed patch and was authorized to continue to its next ticket after acceptance. The next check is due.
evals.expected_output: Surface A's decision while accepting B's supported result and continuing B through its owner. Preserve the project check while it can advance B; a gate in one branch does not stop unrelated work.

evals.name: partial-status-inventory
evals.prompt: The user asks a Poll global controller for an inventory of ten known direct children. Eight snapshot reads succeed; two fail and available history cannot resolve their current status.
evals.expected_output: Report the eight verified states and the two unresolved reads as partial coverage. Do not report all tasks healthy or completed, create replacement owners, or start an ongoing timer solely to conceal the missing results.

evals.name: stale-wakeup-prompt
evals.prompt: A project timer still names old ticket T1 as current, but the controller index and latest task evidence show T1 completed and T2 authorized and active. The user asks to shorten the wakeup prompt.
evals.expected_output: Use a short stable reminder to recover current state; keep changing ticket IDs and progress in the index. Continue with T2 based on current evidence rather than replaying T1. Preserve the existing timer, cadence and notification policy.

evals.name: different-wakeup-recipients
evals.prompt: A project controller checks its workers every 30 minutes. Worker W is waiting for an internal subagent expected to finish in 8 minutes; W has no independent work or its own wakeup. The project check only observes status and does not itself resume W.
evals.expected_output: The project timer does not cover W's internal continuation. W may use an existing suitable self-wakeup or arrange one through codex-async-followup. Avoid a duplicate wakeup to the same recipient and purpose; do not disable the project timer or infer Callback.

evals.name: control-notice-is-not-activity
evals.prompt: The user authorizes handoff only of recently active unfinished tasks. W1 has real recent user discussion. W2 finished weeks ago, but its updated_at is fresh because this controller just sent a handoff notice and renamed it. Decide the handoff set.
evals.expected_output: Use substantive user/work activity from before the bulk operation. W1 qualifies; control-induced timestamps do not reactivate W2 or expand the selection. Inspect W2 history if needed, and do not send another handoff or create its successor based on that notice.

evals.name: handoff-retains-resource-hold
evals.prompt: A Scheduled project is handing off after its timer expires. Worker A still holds the shared test device, B is waiting for the device, and no release or replacement schedule has been authorized. The successor can read the control records.
evals.expected_output: Preserve A's resource hold, B's wait, the expired schedule reference, current authorization and the resumption decision in the transfer context. Ownership acceptance does not release the device, start B, or renew the expired timer. The successor surfaces the unresolved decision.

evals.name: machine-scope-user-title
evals.prompt: The user designates this task as the global controller for Mac mini only and suggests the name 'Mac mini 主控'. A MacBook controller already exists. Establish the role and title.
evals.expected_output: Use the suggested wording in the global controller format, such as '🕹️ Mac mini 主控 · YYYY-MM-DD' with a known stable start date. Record Mac mini as this global controller's scope and preserve the independent MacBook owner. No scope question is needed; a machine scope is not a third controller role.

evals.name: controller-title-does-not-close-role
evals.prompt: The user refers to this ongoing global controller as 'MacBook Coordinator' and prefers English titles. All currently tracked workers finish, but the user has not ended the coordination role or designated a successor.
evals.expected_output: Accept supported worker outcomes and report the empty current workload while retaining the ongoing global controller's 🕹️ role marker, MacBook Coordinator main line, and stable date when available. Do not substitute a worker progress title, mark the controller complete, or create a checkpoint merely because its workers finished.

evals.name: single-machine-global-default
evals.prompt: The user says 'Be my global controller'. Only one machine is known, there is no naming preference, and the conversation is in English.
evals.expected_output: Establish the global role for the available scope without asking a redundant scope question. Use the English default '🕹️ Global Controller' with a stable start date as the recommended second part when available. The controller keeps its role identity through routine work; no fixed Chinese wording or worker focus is required.

evals.name: multiple-machines-optional-alignment
evals.prompt: The user asks you to coordinate their work, without specifying the machine scope. Context shows Mac mini and MacBook, with some already assigned work on Mac mini.
evals.expected_output: Recognize the possible all-machine versus current-machine scope choice. A brief question may help if history does not clarify the preference; it is not a mandatory setup checkpoint. Continue the already assigned Mac mini work without assuming authority for additional machines.

evals.name: project-controller-role-title
evals.prompt: This session is the established Mimo 去重 project controller. It started on 2026-09-14; today is 2026-09-15. Its current title is '🏃 [Android][三源] Mimo 去重项目主控 · 验收机内 mock Gate'. The user says: '按照项目主控规则改 session 名'. A worker is still running the mock acceptance checks. Choose the title.
evals.expected_output: Use the project controller role format, such as '🗂️ Mimo 去重项目主控 · 2026-09-14'. Preserve the project identity and stable start date rather than today's date or the worker's current milestone. The rename neither changes ownership nor claims completion.

evals.name: callback-without-schedule
evals.prompt: The user tells a project controller: 'Have workers tell you when they finish or need my decision.' No periodic checks have been requested. Set the follow-up mode for current and later project tickets.
evals.expected_output: Select Callback for the project's children, supplying only their direct owner's destination and selected events. Apply this child policy to later tickets. Do not create a Scheduled heartbeat or change the project-to-global mode from Poll.

evals.name: controller-wait-with-async-skill
evals.prompt: A global controller has dispatched a project controller that needs 20 minutes to prepare its plan. A separate project controller has dispatched a worker that needs 20 minutes to run tests. Both owners have finished independent work and have codex-async-followup loaded. Neither user has asked for a timer or automatic reports. What should each owner do?
evals.expected_output: Both owners keep Poll, report their dispatch and next evidence, and end their turns until the user next asks. Loading codex-async-followup does not authorize a controller wakeup, including for the child project controller. Dispatched assignments remain in place; neither owner requests a callback.

evals.name: preserve-explicit-mode-scope
evals.prompt: The user previously asked the Billing project controller to check its workers every 30 minutes until project completion. The project receives another authorized ticket. Its global controller has no requested schedule. Establish follow-up for the new ticket and the global controller.
evals.expected_output: Include the ticket in the existing user-selected project schedule without a duplicate timer or new confirmation. Keep the global controller on Poll. The explicit project policy persists only within its scope; no Callback is inferred.

evals.name: switch-scheduled-to-poll
evals.prompt: The user tells a project controller with an active worker-check heartbeat: '以后我来问你时再查，不要定时，也不要让他们主动回报。' One worker is still running and another depends on its result.
evals.expected_output: Switch these child relationships to Poll and pause or remove their controller-check heartbeat and any configured callbacks. Preserve worker assignments and the unresolved dependency; explain that checking the result and coordinating the dependent task will happen on the user's next request. Leave unrelated automations and worker-internal continuation alone.
